{{Short description|International non-governmental organization}} {{EngvarB|date=September 2014}} {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2014}} {{Infobox organization | name = The Elders | image = The Elders Logo.jpg | founded = 18 July 2007 | founder = [[Nelson Mandela]] | location = [[London]] | key_people = [[Juan Manuel Santos]] (Chair)
Alistair Fernie (CEO) | website = {{Official URL}} | purpose = "help resolve some of the world's most intractable [[Group conflict|conflicts]]" and other issues. | num_employees = 18 (as of 2022) | num_members = 12 (including 4 Elders Emeritus) }} [[File:TheElders.jpg|thumb|The Elders (2013)]] '''The Elders''' is an international non-governmental organisation of [[public figure]]s noted as senior statesmen, [[peace activist]]s and [[Human rights activists|human rights advocates]], who were brought together by former president of South Africa [[Nelson Mandela]] in 2007.{{cite web | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/worldnews/1557921/Nelson-Mandela-launches-Elders-to-save-world.html | title=Nelson Mandela launches Elders to save world | date=19 July 2007 }} They describe themselves as "independent global leaders working together for peace, justice, human rights and a sustainable planet". The goal Mandela set for The Elders was to use their "almost 1,000 years of collective experience" to work on solutions for seemingly insurmountable problems such as [[Global warming|climate change]], [[AIDS|HIV/AIDS]], and poverty, as well as to "use their political independence to help resolve some of the world's most intractable [[Group conflict|conflicts]]".{{cite web |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2007/7/19/mandela-unveils-council-of-elders |title=Mandela unveils 'council of elders' - Group including Kofi Annan and Jimmy Carter to tackle some of world's toughest problems. |publisher=[[Al Jazeera]] |date=2007-07-19 |language=en |access-date=2025-02-02}} ==History== As of 2025, The Elders is chaired by [[Juan Manuel Santos]],{{Cite web |title=Juan Manuel Santos, Chair of The Elders |url=https://theelders.org/profile/juan-manuel-santos}} and consists of twelve Elders and four Elders Emeritus.{{Cite web|url=https://theelders.org/news/juan-manuel-santos-named-new-chair-elders|title=Juan Manuel Santos named new Chair of The Elders|website=The Elders|date=2024 |access-date=2025-01-29}}{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/about|title=About The Elders|publisher=TheElders.org|access-date=31 October 2024}} [[Mary Robinson]] served as chair from 2018 until 2024; [[Kofi Annan]] served as chair from 2013 until his death in 2018; [[Desmond Tutu]] served for six years as chair before stepping down in May 2013, and remained an Elder Emeritus until his death in 2021.{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/kofi-annan-appointed-chair-elders |title =Kofi Annan appointed Chair of The Elders |publisher=TheElders.org |date=10 May 2013 |access-date=17 May 2013}} The group was initiated by English philanthropist [[Richard Branson]][http://www.scotsman.com/news/world/branson-planned-mandela-mission-to-prevent-iraq-war-1-1050218 Branson planned Mandela mission to prevent Iraq war], ''[[The Scotsman]]'', 18 December 2004 and musician and human rights activist [[Peter Gabriel]], together with anti-[[apartheid]] activist and former [[President of South Africa|South African President]] [[Nelson Mandela]]. Mandela announced the formation of the group on his eighty-ninth birthday on 18 July 2007 in [[Johannesburg]], South Africa.{{cite web| url= https://www.youtube.com/view_play_list?p=C801BC01AA46FEC2 |title= The Elders press launch in Johannesburg, South Africa |publisher=YouTube |date=18 July 2007 |access-date=26 April 2011}} At the launch ceremony, an empty chair was left on stage for [[Aung San Suu Kyi]], the human rights activist who was a [[political prisoner]] in [[Burma]]/Myanmar at the time. Present at the launch were Kofi Annan, [[Jimmy Carter]], [[Graça Machel]], [[Nelson Mandela]], [[Mary Robinson]], [[Desmond Tutu]], [[Muhammad Yunus]], and [[Li Zhaoxing]]. Members who were not present at the launch were [[Ela Bhatt]], [[Gro Harlem Brundtland]], [[Lakhdar Brahimi]], and [[Fernando Henrique Cardoso]].{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/07/18/world/africa/18safrica.html?_r=1&scp=3&sq=%22the+elders%22+mandela+branson&st=cse|title=Former Leaders Create Freelance Global Diplomatic Team|first=Michael|last=Wines|work=The New York Times |date=18 July 2007 }} [[Martti Ahtisaari]] joined The Elders in September 2009, [[Hina Jilani]] and [[Ernesto Zedillo]] in July 2013,{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/martti-ahtisaari-joins-elders|title=Martti Ahtisaari joins The Elders|website=The Elders|date=21 September 2009 }} and [[Ricardo Lagos]] in June 2016.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/former-president-chile-ricardo-lagos-join-elders|title=Former President of Chile Ricardo Lagos to join The Elders|website=The Elders|date=30 June 2016 }} In June 2017, former UN Secretary-General [[Ban Ki-moon]] also joined the group.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/former-un-secretary-general-ban-ki-moon-joins-elders|title=Former UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon joins The Elders|website=The Elders|date=30 June 2017 }} [[Zeid Raad Al Hussein]], [[Juan Manuel Santos]] and [[Ellen Johnson Sirleaf]] joined The Elders in January 2019. [[Tsakhiagiin Elbegdorj|Elbegdorj Tsakhia]], former President and Prime Minister of Mongolia, joined in October 2022. [[Princess Mabel of Orange-Nassau|Mabel van Oranje]], former CEO of The Elders, sits on the advisory council in her capacity as Advisory Committee Chair of ''[[Girls Not Brides]]''.{{cite web |url= http://theelders.org/about/donors |title= The Elders: Donors |publisher= TheElders.org |access-date= 25 April 2013 |archive-date= 9 May 2013 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130509041051/http://theelders.org/about/donors |url-status= dead }} The Elders publish annual reports detailing the organisation's income and spending activity.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/sites/default/files/the-elders-annual-report-2015-final.pdf |title=Annual report |date=2015 |website=theelders.org }} ==Work== The Elders say they use their independence, collective experience and influence to work for peace, justice, human rights and a sustainable planet. In their 2023–27 Strategy, The Elders' focus will be on three existential threats – the climate crisis, nuclear weapons and pandemics – and the continuing scourge of conflict.{{cite web |url=https://theelders.org/what-we-do |title=What we do - We work on existential threats to humanity that require a collective response - the climate crisis, pandemics, and nuclear weapons. We also work on conflict, a threat in itself and a risk factor for other threats. |publisher=TheElders.org |date=2024 |language=en |access-date=2025-02-02}} The Elders also have four cross-cutting commitments across all initiatives: human rights, gender equality and women's leadership, [[multilateralism]] and intergenerational dialogue.{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} ===Current work=== ==== The climate crisis ==== In 2023–2027, The Elders say they will aim to hold big emitters to account for policies that align with the 1.5 °C limit and the global nature goal, and accelerate just transitions. They say will seek to influence the shape of the new [[climate finance]] goal to be agreed by 2025, and push for implementation of the UN agreement to operationalise a loss and damage fund. The Elders have expressed support the re-engineering of global [[development finance institution]]s to raise trillions of dollars for tackling the climate crisis, and say they want to see the voices of youth and women heard and respected so that a new political space can be created for more ambitious climate actions.{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} ==== Pandemics ==== The Elders have said they will advocate for a robust global PPR (Pandemic Preparedness and Response) agenda that should be treated as a global public good, requiring global public investment. They say that tackling pandemics must involve all parts of society, government, and the economy, and resilient and that publicly funded health systems based on the principles of [[Universal health care|Universal Health Coverage]] (UHC) are crucial.{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} ==== Nuclear weapons ==== The Elders say their goal is a world where current and future generations are free from the threat of nuclear destruction. They say they will use their moral voice to challenge world leaders, embolden multilateral approaches, and mobilise [[civil society]]. This includes advocating for more voices to be heard in decision-making, particularly women and youth.{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} ==== Conflict ==== The Elders say they will focus their efforts on advocating for international law and accountability, and on engagement in a limited number of conflict situations where they are they have the ability to play a distinctive role. They have said they initially plan to prioritise [[Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russia’s war on Ukraine]] and the [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict|Israeli-Palestinian conflict]].{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} On 20 October 2023 Mary Robinson discussed with representatives of [[Office of the President of Ukraine|Ukrainian President's Office]] implementation of [[Ukrainian Peace Formula]].{{Cite web |title=Representatives of President's Office discuss implementation of Ukrainian Peace Formula with Head of The Elders Mary Robinson |url=https://www.president.gov.ua/en/news/predstavniki-ofisu-prezidenta-obgovorili-z-ochilniceyu-grupi-86505}} On 1 December 2023 President The Elders took part in a working meeting with representatives of 83 states on the implementation of the [[Ukraine's Peace Formula|Ukrainian Peace Formula]] in Kyiv, Ukraine.{{Cite web |title=Андрій Єрмак 🇺🇦 |url=https://t.me/ermaka2022/4073 |access-date=2023-12-02 |website=Telegram}} ===Past work=== ==== Universal health care (2016–2022) ==== At the [[Women Deliver]] conference in May 2016, The Elders launched a new initiative to campaign for [[Universal health care|universal health coverage]] (UHC) as part of their efforts to support and implement the UN [[Sustainable Development Goals]] (SDGs).{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-launch-new-initiative-universal-health-coverage-women-deliver|title=The Elders launch new initiative on Universal Health Coverage at Women Deliver|website=The Elders|date=17 May 2016 }} The initiative focused on four areas: # Promoting UHC as the best way to achieve the health Sustainable Development Goal.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/faqs-uhc-and-sustainable-development-goals|title=UHC explained: Universal Health Coverage and the Sustainable Development Goals|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427003635/http://theelders.org/article/faqs-uhc-and-sustainable-development-goals|url-status=dead}} # Promoting UHC's health, economic and political benefits;{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/faqs-uhc-delivers-substantial-health-economic-and-political-benefits|title=UHC explained: Universal Health Coverage delivers substantial health, economic and political benefits|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427095926/http://theelders.org/article/faqs-uhc-delivers-substantial-health-economic-and-political-benefits|url-status=dead}} # Prioritising women, children and adolescents in UHC's implementation; # Reiterating the role of public financing in sustainably funding UHC.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/faqs-public-financing-key-uhc|title=UHC explained: Public financing is the key to UHC|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427100315/http://theelders.org/article/faqs-public-financing-key-uhc|url-status=dead}} In September 2016, Gro Harlem Brundtland delivered a keynote speech at a high-level event on the sidelines of the 71st UN General Assembly in New York.{{cite web | title=High-level meetings of the 71st session of the UN General Assembly | publisher=United Nations | url=https://www.un.org/en/ga/71/meetings/ | access-date=May 24, 2026}} Joined by [[Margaret Chan]], Director-General of the [[WHO]] and health ministers of South Africa and Thailand, she called for courageous leadership to achieve Universal Health Coverage by 2030.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/accelerating-progress-toward-uhc-2030|title=Accelerating progress toward UHC by 2030|website=The Elders|date=24 October 2016 }} In January 2017, Kofi Annan sent letters to Indian leaders to commend the progress made in reforming the Indian healthcare system,{{cite web|url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/delhi/after-kofi-annan-former-norway-pm-praises-aap-govt-s-mohalla-clinics/story-PErXELux8KNYtyT7wLQ4uM.html|title=After Kofi Annan, another world leader praises AAP govt's mohalla clinics|date=2 February 2017}}{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-urge-bold-steps-reach-universal-health-coverage-india|title=The Elders urge bold steps to reach Universal Health Coverage in India|website=The Elders|date=26 January 2017 }} and Gro Harlem Brundtland and Ernesto Zedillo delivered keynote speeches at the Prince Mahidol Awards Conference in Bangkok, Thailand. Gro Harlem Brundtland highlighted the importance of inclusive health policy{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/social-inclusion-what-does-it-mean-health-policy-and-practice|title=Social Inclusion: What Does It Mean for Health Policy and Practice?|website=The Elders|date=February 2017 }} and Ernesto Zedillo explained how to sustainably implement Universal Health Coverage.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/four-pillars-ensure-inclusive-uhc|title=Four pillars to ensure inclusive UHC|website=The Elders|date=2 February 2017 }} Highlighting the link between access to affordable health care and gender equality, in January 2017, two members of The Elders expressed concern at the re-introduction of the [[Mexico City policy|Mexico City Policy]] by the recently inaugurated [[President of the United States]], [[Donald Trump]]. The pro-abortion activist Gro Harlem Brundtland said: "This decision puts the health of women and children at risk" and warned that "vulnerable people will die unnecessarily."{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-statement-us-reintroduction-global-gag-rule|title=The Elders' statement on US reintroduction of "Global Gag Rule"|website=The Elders|date=30 January 2017 }} ====Refugees and migration==== In October 2015, Kofi Annan, Gro Brundtland and Hina Jilani joined [[Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights|UN High Commissioner for Human Rights]] [[Prince Zeid bin Ra'ad|Prince Zeid Ra'ad Al Hussein]] and [[William L. Swing]], the Director General of the [[International Organization for Migration]], at an event on the refugee and migration crisis at the [[Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies|Graduate Institute]] in Geneva. During the event, Gro Harlem Brundtland said "Too many leaders are not only shy when it comes to making this case to their people, they fundamentally lack the courage to do so...". Prince Zeid Ra'ad Al Hussein also rejected the dehumanising rhetoric adopted by some politicians towards refugees and migrants.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/show-political-courage-over-refugee-crisis|title=Show political courage over the refugee crisis|website=The Elders|date=28 October 2015 }} Ahead of the UN Summit for Refugees and Migrants in September 2016, Kofi Annan, Maarti Ahtisaari and Lakhdar Brahimi visited Germany to launch a report calling for stronger political will to ensure that responsibility is truly shared between countries, and for better protection of the vulnerable. They met the then-Foreign Minister [[Frank-Walter Steinmeier]], and Federal President [[Joachim Gauck]], and also visited a refugee resettlement centre in Berlin to hear directly from new arrivals to Germany.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-hail-germanys-engagement-refugee-and-migration-issues|title=The Elders hail Germany's engagement on refugee and migration issues|website=The Elders|date=13 September 2016 }} The report "In Challenge Lies Opportunity: How the world must respond to refugees and mass migration" outlined four key principles which The Elders believe should be at the heart of the international response to refugees and mass migration:{{cite web | title=In Challenge Lies Opportunity: How the World Must Respond to Refugees and Mass Migration | website=The Elders | date=September 13, 2016 | url=https://theelders.org/news/challenge-lies-opportunity-how-world-must-respond-refugees-and-mass-migration | access-date=May 24, 2026}} # Response mechanisms to large flows of people must be developed and properly coordinated, both regionally and internationally # Assistance to major refugee-hosting countries must be enhanced # Resettlement opportunities must be increased, along with additional pathways for admission # Human rights and refugee protection must be upheld and strengthened Three Elders attended the UN Summit for Refugees and Migrants on 19 September 2016, which was held during the 71st Session of the [[United Nations General Assembly|United Nations' General Assembly]].{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-visit-unga-high-level-week-new-york-17-22-september-2016|title=Elders' Visit to UNGA High-Level Week, New York, 17-22 September 2016|website=The Elders|date=31 October 2016 }} Martti Ahtisaari, Hina Jilani and Mary Robinson spoke at the high-level Round Tables which addressed different aspects of the topic: vulnerabilities of refugees and migrants, responsibility-sharing and respect for international law, and addressing the drivers of migration, respectively. In January 2017, The Elders condemned the US [[Executive Order 13769|refugee ban]], enacted by the recently inaugurated President of the United States, Donald J. Trump. Kofi Annan said: "It is deeply regrettable that a nation of immigrants should turn its back so harshly on refugees escaping violence and war.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-condemn-us-refugee-ban-call-global-protection-vulnerable|title=The Elders condemn US refugee ban, call for global protection of vulnerable|website=The Elders|date=31 January 2017 }} ====Stronger UN==== At the [[Munich Security Conference]] in February 2015, the Elders launched the "Stronger UN" initiative, which promoted a series of reforms to strengthen the [[United Nations]]. This included a review of the composition of the [[United Nations Security Council|Security Council]] and of the appointment of the [[Secretary-General of the United Nations|Secretary-General]].{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/elders-call-strengthening-united-nations|title=The Elders call for strengthening of the United Nations|website=The Elders|date=7 February 2015 }} Noting that seventy years since its founding, the UN was still falling short of its Charter pledge "to save succeeding generations from the scourge of war", The Elders proposed to: # Make the Security Council more representative of the world today, by introducing a new category of non-permanent members that can be immediately re-elected if they obtained the trust of the other members. As such, they would become de facto permanent members.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/un-fit-purpose|title=A UN fit for purpose|website=The Elders|access-date=29 June 2015|archive-date=1 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701004133/http://theelders.org/un-fit-purpose|url-status=dead}} # Break the deadlock in the Security Council in situations of atrocity crimes by compelling [[Permanent members of the United Nations Security Council|P-5 member]]s to pledge that they will not use or threaten to use their veto in case of humanitarian crisis where people are victims of [[genocide]] or other atrocities. # Urge the Security Council to make more regular and systematic use of the "[[Arria formula meeting|Arria formula]]" to give groups representing people in zones of conflict the opportunity to inform and influence Council decisions. # Make the selection process of the Secretary-General more transparent and fair At the [[World Humanitarian Summit]] in May 2016, several Elders featured in a video alongside [[Salil Shetty]], Secretary-General of [[Amnesty International]] and Simon Adams, Executive-Director of the [[Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect|Global Center for the Responsibility to Protect]], calling for veto restraint and increased cooperation amongst the [[Permanent members of the United Nations Security Council|Permanent Members of the UN Security Council]] to prevent mass atrocities and save lives.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/ahead-world-humanitarian-summit-elders-urge-un-action-stop-mass-atrocities|title=Ahead of World Humanitarian Summit, The Elders urge UN action to stop mass atrocities|website=The Elders|date=20 May 2016 }} In 2016, some of The Elders' recommendations on the selection of the new Secretary-General were adopted by the UN. For the first time, the names of candidates for the position of Secretary-General were publicly circulated, and all declared candidates participated in public hearings in the General Assembly. These changes led to a notable increase in the transparency of the selection process.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-welcome-nomination-antonio-guterres-next-un-secretary-general|title=The Elders welcome nomination of António Guterres as next UN Secretary-General|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427100327/http://theelders.org/article/elders-welcome-nomination-antonio-guterres-next-un-secretary-general|url-status=dead}} ====Climate change==== Prior to the [[2009 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] in Copenhagen, The Elders launched the Climate Change initiative together with their grandchildren.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-enlist-their-grandchildrens-help-climate-change|title=The Elders enlist their grandchildren's help on climate change|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427100525/http://theelders.org/article/elders-enlist-their-grandchildrens-help-climate-change|url-status=dead}} The Elders believe that strong leadership is required at all levels in order to deliver a sustainable future. They strongly welcomed the [[Paris Agreement|Paris Agreement on Climate Change]] reached at the [[2015 United Nations Climate Change Conference|COP21]] summit in December 2015, and are working to ensure it is now implemented fully and fairly. The Elders believe that as climate change goes hand in hand with sustainable development, a holistic policy approach that is able to incorporate the voice of civil society and grassroots activities is needed. In this regard, in 2012, The Elders engaged with four young activists in an inter-generational debate on the change needed to secure a sustainable future for the planet, in the run-up to the [[United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development|UN Conference on Sustainable Development]] (Rio+20).{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/eldersyoungers-building-sustainable-and-more-equitable-world-all|title=Elders+Youngers: building a sustainable and more equitable world for all|website=The Elders|date=14 August 2012 }} Similarly, in 2016, Elders such as Mary Robinson and Gro Harlem Brundtland participated in the Social Good Summit in New York, in which they took part in dialogues with global climate and young activists.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/bad-weather-human-cost-climate-change|title=Bad weather: The Human Cost of Climate Change|website=The Elders|date=25 October 2016 }} While The Elders condemned the announcement in June 2017 by President Trump of his intention to withdraw from the Paris Agreement,{{cite web|url=https://www.theelders.org/article/elders-condemn-us-quitting-paris-climate-agreement-no-one-country-can-dismantle-it|title=The Elders condemn US for quitting Paris climate agreement: no one country can dismantle it.|website=The Elders|date=June 2017 |access-date=2018-02-06}} they note that this has in fact galvanised action by states and cities. They maintain the need to hold governments and businesses to their word so that the deal is implemented in full and in good faith, with adequate means to ratchet up ambition and have reiterated this in subsequent meetings including with [[Pope Francis]] and [[Emmanuel Macron|President Macron]] in late 2017.{{cite web|url=https://www.theelders.org/climate-change|title=Climate change|website=The Elders|access-date=2018-02-06}} In 2023, in advance of [[COP28]] in Dubai, the group released a statement outlining their call for meaningful climate action.{{Cite web |date=2023-08-30 |title=The Elders' calls to action for COP28 |url=https://theelders.org/news/elders-calls-action-cop28 |access-date=2023-12-05 |website=theelders.org |language=en}} After some controversial remarks by COP president [[Sultan Al Jaber]] during the early December gathering, Elders chair Mary Robinson, writing on social media, repeated the need to stop burning fossil fuels and adopt renewable energy.{{Cite news |last=Hanman |first=Natalie |date=2023-12-05 |title='The science compels: phase out fossil fuels' – Mary Robinson responds after Cop28 row – live |language=en-GB |work=the Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/live/2023/dec/05/cop28-live-energy-in-focus-after-scientists-reject-presidents-fossil-fuel-comments |access-date=2023-12-05 |issn=0261-3077 |quote=Mary Robinson has made her first comment since the row over the Cop28 president’s controversial and ill-tempered response to her questions on the need for a fossil fuel phase out… "The science compels: phase out fossil fuels rapidly, accelerate renewable energy adoption, and radically scaled up finance.”}} ====Equality for women and girls==== Commitment to gender equality is a cornerstone of The Elders' engagement in securing dignity and rights for all. From Universal Health Coverage to climate change and mass migration, to peacebuilding and protecting human rights defenders, The Elders believe that women and girls have specific needs that demand appropriately-tailored policy responses. This includes considering the impact of religion and tradition on women's rights,{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/religious-and-traditional-practices-discriminate-against-women-and-girls|title=Religious and traditional practices discriminate against women and girls|website=The Elders|date=2 July 2009 }} addressing the harmful practice of [[child marriage]], supporting efforts to promote women as [[peacemakers]],{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/you-cannot-have-sustainable-peace-without-women|title="You cannot have sustainable peace without women"|website=The Elders|date=7 November 2014 }} highlighting the specific burdens and responsibilities women face in societies most threatened by climate change, highlighting the scale of violence against women,{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/violence-against-women-increasing-public-awareness|title=Violence against women – increasing public awareness|website=The Elders|date=24 November 2014 }} end impunity for sexual violence|website=The Elders|date=13 June 2014 }} – including [[United Nations peacekeeping#Crimes by peacekeepers|exploitation by UN Peacekeeping missions]]{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-welcome-un-secretary-generals-commitment-fight-sexual-exploitation|title=The Elders welcome UN Secretary-General's commitment to fight sexual exploitation|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April the health needs of women in the implementation of Universal Health Coverage.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/why-must-women-children-adolescents-be-uhc-priority|title=Why must women, children & adolescents be a UHC priority?|website=The Elders|date=11 October 2016 }} In July 2009 The Elders called for an end to harmful and discriminatory practices that are justified on the grounds
