We ask, in particular, that leaders of all religions have the courage to acknowledge and emphasise the positive messages of dignity and equality that all the world's major faiths share".{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/01/10/opinion/10kristof.html?ref=opinion|title=Opinion – Religion and Women|first=Nicholas|last=Kristof|work=The New York Times |date=10 January 2010 }} ''New York Times'' columnist [[Nicholas Kristof]] later wrote that "The Elders are right that religious groups should stand up for a simple ethical principle: any person's human rights should be sacred, and not depend on something as earthly as their genitals."{{cite web|url=https://www.icrw.org/child-marriage-facts-and-figures/|title=Child Marriage Facts and Figures – ICRW – PASSION. PROOF. POWER.|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=10 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230610012709/https://www.icrw.org/child-marriage-facts-and-figures/|url-status=dead}} ====Elders+Youngers==== When Nelson Mandela founded The Elders in 2007, he told the group to listen to the marginalised – especially young people. The Elders' work with young people has consisted in meeting many passionate young people on peace, equality and protecting the environment. In 2012, The Elders and four young activists began an inter-generational debate about the change needed to secure a sustainable future, in the run-up to the [[United Nations Conference on Sustainable Development|UN Conference on Sustainable Development]] (Rio+20). Beside collaborating with young climate activists, The Elders have also held roundtable discussions on African leadership, debated [[2011 Egyptian revolution|Egypt's revolution]] with young people in Cairo, discussed the refugee crisis and UN reform with young students at [[Sciences Po]] in Paris and, featured guest blogs from youth contributors on their website.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/africa-2010-game-plan-winning-continent|title=Africa 2010: A Game Plan for a Winning Continent|website=The Elders|date=29 May 2010 }}{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-egyptian-youth-you-are-future|title=Elders to Egyptian youth: "You are the future"|website=The Elders|date=29 October 2012 }}{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/lakhdar-brahimi-discuss-migration-and-security-sciences-po|title=Lakhdar Brahimi to discuss migration and security at Sciences Po|website=The Elders|date=13 January 2017 }}{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/martti-ahtisaari-calls-un-reform-sciences-po-event-paris|title=Martti Ahtisaari calls for UN reform at Sciences Po event in Paris|website=The Elders|date=18 January 2016 }}{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/news-media/elders-youngers/guest-blog|title=News & Media|website=The Elders|date=26 March 2013 }} ====Iran==== The Elders support greater openness and dialogue between Iran and the international community, and encourage Iran to play a stabilising role in the wider Middle East. In their first visit to Iran as a group, The Elders travelled to [[Tehran]] in January 2014 to meet privately with the Iranian leadership.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-conclude-fruitful-first-visit-iran|title=The Elders conclude fruitful first visit to Iran|website=The Elders|date=30 January 2014 }} Delegation leader Kofi Annan and fellow Elders Martti Ahtisaari, Desmond Tutu and Ernesto Zedillo held a series of productive meetings on the easing of regional tensions; the spread of extremist violence internationally; human rights; and the Syrian crisis. They were encouraged by Iran's new spirit of openness and dialogue with the outside world. In February 2015, The Elders met again with Foreign Minister [[Mohammad Javad Zarif|Javad Zarif]], on the margins of the [[Munich Security Conference]], to encourage a successful conclusion of the [[P5+1]] nuclear negotiations and to discuss solutions to regional security issues. In July 2015, The Elders welcomed the [[Iran nuclear deal framework|agreement reached on Iran's nuclear programme]] between Iran, the P5+1 countries (US, Russia, China, UK, France and Germany) and the [[EU]].{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-welcome-iranian-nuclear-agreement-boost-middle-east-peace|title=The Elders welcome Iranian nuclear agreement as boost to Middle East peace|website=The Elders|date=14 July 2015 }} They believe the agreement represents a historic opportunity to end decades of animosity between Iran and the West, especially the US, and to rebuild relationships on the basis of trust and mutual respect. In 2016, The Elders issued a press release welcoming the lifting of [[sanctions against Iran]] as part of the implementation of the P5+1 nuclear deal, the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action]], which they continued to support throughout the year.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-welcome-lifting-sanctions-against-iran|title=The Elders welcome the lifting of sanctions against Iran|website=The Elders|date=20 January 2016 }} In January 2017, The Elders issued a statement following the death of former Iranian President [[Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani|Rafsanjani]], stating that "Iran has lost one of its most influential leaders and a strong voice for reform and for the improvement of regional relations."{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-statement-death-former-iranian-president-rafsanjani|title=The Elders' statement on the death of former Iranian President Rafsanjani|website=The Elders|date=12 January 2017 }} At the Munich Security Conference in February 2017 Ernesto Zedillo and Lakhdar Brahimi met again with Javad Zarif. They also hosted a panel debate to defend the Iran Nuclear Agreement, joined by [[Turki bin Faisal Al Saud|HRH Prince Turki]] of Saudi Arabia and [[Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani|Sheikh Hamad of Qatar.]]{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/iran-nuclear-agreement-deal-worth-keeping|title=The Iran Nuclear Agreement: A Deal Worth Keeping?|website=The Elders|date=20 February 2017 }} At the start of the [[2026 Iran war]], Juan Manuel Santos issued a statement calling for deescalation and argued that the United States and Israel's strikes "violate[d] international law and threaten regional and global security."{{Cite web |date=2026-02-28 |title=Chair of The Elders appeals for de-escalation in Iran conflict |url=https://theelders.org/news/chair-elders-appeals-de-escalation-iran-conflict |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=theelders.org |language=en}} A subsequent full statement form the Elders stated that the conflict "threaten[s] grave consequences for regional security and the global economy"{{Cite web |date=2026-03-18 |title=War in Iran: Elders call for consistency in defence of the international rule of law |url=https://theelders.org/news/war-iran-elders-call-consistency-defence-international-rule-law |access-date=2026-04-08 |website=theelders.org |language=en}} ====Israel and Palestine==== The long-running [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]] has been one of The Elders' top priorities since the group was founded. Given the far-reaching impact of the unresolved conflict and the power imbalance between the parties, The Elders believe the international community has a vital role to play in helping Israelis and Palestinians reach a lasting solution. Particularly, they insist that the peace efforts must be based on the respect for universal human rights and international humanitarian law, as well as that the siege on [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] must be permanently lifted and that the boundaries between Israel and a viable Palestinian state must be based on the 1967 borders, including a Palestinian capital in [[East Jerusalem]].{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/israel-palestine|title=Israel-Palestine|website=The Elders}} In this regard, in August 2009, The Elders visited [[Israel]] and the [[West Bank]] to draw attention to the impact of the long-running conflict on ordinary people, and to support efforts by Israelis and Palestinians to promote peace.{{cite web|url=https://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/business/richard-branson-without-mideast-resolution-something-ghastly-could-happen-1.282760|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100811225509/http://www.haaretz.com/print-edition/business/richard-branson-without-mideast-resolution-something-ghastly-could-happen-1.282760|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 August 2010|title=Richard Branson: Without Mideast Resolution, 'Something Ghastly' Could Happen|first1=Mike|last1=Dagan|first2=Guy|last2=Rolnik|first3=Asher |last3=Schechter|date=27 August 2009|work=Haaretz}} They were joined on the trip by Richard Branson and Jeff Skoll.{{cite web|url=https://www.haaretz.com/news/elders-of-peace-israel-must-freeze-west-bank-settlements-1.282718|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606203226/http://www.haaretz.com/news/elders-of-peace-israel-must-freeze-west-bank-settlements-1.282718|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 June 2011|title=Elders of Peace: Israel Must Freeze West Bank Settlements|date=26 August 2009|work=Haaretz}} The Elders met Israeli President [[Shimon Peres]], Palestinian Prime Minister [[Salam Fayyad]],{{cite web|author=By ETHAN BRONNERAUG. 27, 2009 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/08/28/world/middleeast/28bilin.html?_r=2 |title=In Village, Palestinians See Model for Their Cause |work=The New York Times |date=2009-08-27 |access-date=2018-08-18}} and local peace activists involved in non-violent demonstrations. The report of their visit said they hoped it would "spur leaders and ordinary citizens alike to actions that will further peace, human rights and justice for all in the Middle East".{{cite web|url=http://www.maannews.com/Content.aspx?ID=324344|title=Ex-leaders of US, Ireland to visit region|agency=Maan News Agency}} Four Elders, Mary Robinson, Ela Bhatt, Lakhdar Brahimi, and Jimmy Carter, returned to the Middle East in October 2010 to visit [[Egypt]], Gaza, Israel, [[Jordan]], [[Syria]] and the West Bank. The aim was to encourage peace efforts{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-mideast-carter-idUSTRE69D5PD20101014|title=Ex-President Carter to start Mideast peace tour|website=[[Reuters]] |date=14 October 2010 }} with an emphasis on the need to reach "a just and secure peace for all" based on [[international law]].{{cite web|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2010/WORLD/meast/10/21/israel.elders.visit/|title='Elders' visit Israel on Mideast peace tour|publisher=CNN}} Throughout the trip, The Elders held discussions on the [[Israeli–Palestinian peace process|peace process]] with political leaders, representatives of human rights organisations, student and youth groups, women's groups, business, civil society and opinion leaders. During the trip, Mary Robinson said that "As Elders, we believe the [[two-state solution]] has the potential to deliver peace – but a more energetic and comprehensive approach is needed."{{cite web|url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/carter-in-syria-israel-must-fully-lift-gaza-blockade-1.320044|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160121074541/http://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/carter-in-syria-israel-must-fully-lift-gaza-blockade-1.320044|url-status=dead|archive-date=21 January 2016|title=Carter in Syria: Israel Must Fully Lift Gaza Blockade|date=19 October 2010|work=Haaretz}} The Elders also called for an immediate end to the [[Blockade of the Gaza Strip]], describing it as an "illegal collective punishment" and "an impediment to peace." The Elders released a report outlining their conclusions following the visit, which they hoped would "be a helpful contribution to peace efforts."{{cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/Diplomacy-and-Politics/Elders-meet-Peres-over-stalemate-in-peace-process|title=Elders meet Peres over stalemate in peace process|work=Jerusalem Post|date=21 October 2012 }} In October 2012, Gro Harlem Brundtland, Jimmy Carter and Mary Robinson returned to the region, travelling to Israel, the West Bank and Egypt.{{cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/news/jimmy-carter-says-mideast-peace-vanishing-155117602.html|title=Jimmy Carter says Mideast peace is 'vanishing'|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427004838/https://www.yahoo.com/news/jimmy-carter-says-mideast-peace-vanishing-155117602.html|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/we-are-heading-towards-one-state-outcome|title='We are heading towards a one-state outcome'|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2013|archive-date=11 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131211034153/http://www.theelders.org/article/we-are-heading-towards-one-state-outcome|url-status=dead}} In their discussions with political leaders, civil society, and humanitarian and human rights experts, the Elders sought to "express concern about the future of the [[two-state solution]] and highlight the effect of [[Israeli settlement|settlement]] expansion and other changes in the city of [[Jerusalem]] as a major impediment to peace between Israelis and Palestinians."{{cite web|url=https://www.businesslive.co.za/bd/|title=Business Day|website=www.businesslive.co.za}} In May 2015, Jimmy Carter and Gro Harlem Brundtland visited Israel and Palestine and ended their visit to Israel and Palestine with a call for meaningful steps to stop the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and reconcile the different Palestinian factions. They held talks with President [[Mahmoud Abbas]] and senior political figures from both Israel and Palestine, civil society groups and ordinary citizens to hear their perspectives and convey The Elders' commitment to a fair and enduring resolution to the conflict.{{Cite web |url=https://shmuley.com/2016/01/25/whats-richard-bransons-problem-with-israel/ |title=Rabbi Shmuley | JP: What's Richard Branson's Problem with Israel? |access-date=25 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201011327/https://shmuley.com/2016/01/25/whats-richard-bransons-problem-with-israel/ |archive-date=1 February 2016 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }} The Elders supported the diplomatic efforts led by the French Government to keep the two-state solution alive through high-level conferences in Paris in June 2016 and in January 2017. They also welcomed the [[Occupied Palestine Resolution|UN Security Council Resolution in December 2016]] that called on Israel to immediately halt all [[Israeli settlement|settlement activity]] in the occupied Palestinian territories.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-welcome-paris-mideast-peace-conference-urge-all-p5-states-show-leadership|title=The Elders welcome Paris Mideast peace conference, urge all P5 states to show leadership|website=The Elders|date=16 January 2017 }} They fully support the [[Arab Peace Initiative]],{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/qa-arab-peace-initiative|title=Q&A: the Arab Peace Initiative|website=The Elders|date=10 September 2013 }} which calls for normal, peaceful and secure relations between Israel and the Arab world, in return for Israeli withdrawal from Palestinian territory occupied since 1967. In 2017, The Elders condemned Donald Trump's decision to recognise [[Jerusalem]] as the capital of Israel stating this "greatly harms peace processes."{{cite web|url=https://theelders.org/article/elders-condemn-us-recognition-jerusalem-israeli-capital-grave-risk-peace|title=The Elders condemn US recognition of Jerusalem as Israeli capital as grave risk to peace|website=The Elders|date=6 December 2017 }} In November 2023, weeks into the deadly and bloody [[Gaza war]], The Elders released a letter calling on U.S. President [[Joe Biden]] to "set out a serious peace plan, and help build a new coalition for peace to deliver it".{{Cite web |date=2023-11-16 |title=Dear President Biden: The Elders' open letter on Israel and Palestine |url=https://theelders.org/news/dear-president-biden-elders-open-letter-israel-and-palestine |access-date=2023-11-19 |website=theelders.org |language=en |quote=De-escalation is not enough. We cannot go back to managing the conflict. It will erupt again and again with more death and misery. The conflict must be resolved, permanently, through negotiation.}} ====Myanmar==== A delegation of Elders visited [[Myanmar]] for the first time as a group in September 2013. In their meetings with senior officials in the government, political leaders, religious leaders and civil society groups, Martti Ahtisaari, Gro Harlem Brundtland and Jimmy Carter explored how best they could support peace and inclusive development in the country.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-encourage-all-parties-myanmar-advance-national-reforms-support-peace-accords|title=The Elders encourage all parties in Myanmar to advance national reforms, support peace accords|website=The Elders|date=26 September 2013 }}{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/myanmars-grassroots-should-have-role-national-reforms-peace-talks|title=Myanmar's grassroots should have a role in national reforms, peace talks|website=The Elders|access-date=7 September 2015|archive-date=31 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151031105859/http://theelders.org/article/myanmars-grassroots-should-have-role-national-reforms-peace-talks|url-status=dead}} The Elders returned to Myanmar in March and December 2014. In the first trip, they travelled to [[Naypyidaw|Nay Pyi Taw]] and [[Myitkyina|Myitkyina, Kachin State]], in Myanmar and to [[Mae Sot]] and [[Chiang Mai]] in Thailand and deepened their relations key interlocutors and focused particularly on representatives of the country's ethnic minorities.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-call-immediate-end-conflict-myanmar-and-urge-parties-engage-talks|title=The Elders call for immediate end to conflict in Myanmar and urge parties to engage in talks|website=The Elders|date=18 December 2014 }} In the second one, they visited [[Yangon]] and Nay Pyi Taw in Myanmar and Chiang Mai in Thailand, and they reaffirmed their efforts to encourage sustained progress in Myanmar's transition process and called for an immediate end to the conflict.{{Cite web |url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-cyprus-talks-carter-idUKTRE48P20D20080926 |title=Former U.S. President Carter and Tutu to visit Cyprus |access-date=26 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427095826/http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-cyprus-talks-carter-idUKTRE48P20D20080926 |archive-date=27 April 2017 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }} The Elders welcomed the elections in Myanmar in November 2015 and the victory of [[Aung San Suu Kyi|Aung San Suu Kyi']]s [[National League for Democracy]] (NLD) in forming a civilian-led government. In August 2016, Aung San Suu Kyi invited Kofi Annan to chair an independent Commission to assess the situation in [[Rakhine State]], including the [[Rohingya people|Rohingya]] community. The Commission published its final report in August 2017 and put forward recommendations to surmount the political, socio-economic and humanitarian challenges that currently face Rakhine State. On publishing the report, Kofi Annan said: "Unless concerted action – led by the government and aided by all sectors of the government and society – is taken soon, we risk the return of another cycle of violence and radicalisation, which will further deepen the chronic poverty that afflicts Rakhine State." The Elders supported Kofi Annan in this role, which he undertook in his own capacity. At their October 2017 board meeting, The Elders issued a statement{{cite web|url=https://www.theelders.org/article/elders-call-myanmar-allow-return-displaced-rohingya|title=The Elders call on Myanmar to allow return of displaced Rohingya|website=The Elders|date=25 October 2017 |access-date=2018-02-06}} expressing their deep dismay and concern at the wave of [[Rohingya genocide|violence and destruction]] that swept through Rakhine State from August 2017, displacing hundreds of thousands of Rohingya Muslims. They called on Myanmar's government and military leaders to allow [[Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh|displaced Rohingya in Bangladesh]] and other countries to return, and for their human rights and safety to be protected.{{cite web|url=https://www.theelders.org/myanmar|title=Myanmar|website=The Elders|access-date=2018-02-06}} ====Zimbabwe==== [[Zimbabwe]] has been a key focus of concern for The Elders since the group was formed in 2007. Once one of Africa's strongest economies, Zimbabwe has suffered sustained political and economic crises over the last two decades and its leaders are failing in their responsibilities to the country's people. In November 2008, three members of the Elders – Jimmy Carter, Graça Machel and Kofi Annan – planned to visit Zimbabwe to draw attention to the country's escalating humanitarian and economic crises.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-cancel-visit-zimbabwe-meetings-continue-south-africa|title=The Elders cancel visit to Zimbabwe: meetings to continue in South Africa|website=The Elders}} A day before their planned travel to [[Harare]], they were informed that they would be refused entry.{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2008/nov/22/zimbabwe|title=Jimmy Carter and Kofi Annan refused entry visas to Zimabwe|agency=Associated Press|date=22 November 2008|website=the Guardian}} Jimmy Carter said it was the first time he had been denied permission [link] to enter any country.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/11/23/world/africa/23zimbabwe.html|title=Carter Group Barred From Zimbabwe|first=Celia W.|last=Dugger|work=The New York Times |date=22 November 2008 }} The three Elders stayed in [[Johannesburg]] and were briefed by Zimbabwean political and business leaders, aid workers, donors, UN agencies and civil society representatives, many of whom travelled from Zimbabwe to see them. The Elders also held meetings with the leaders of South Africa and Botswana.{{cite web|url=https://mg.co.za/article/2008-11-24-elders-zim-crisis-beyond-what-we-could-have-imagined|title=Elders: Zim crisis 'beyond what we could have imagined'|first=Thembela|last=Khamango|date=24 November 2008 }} At a press conference after their meetings, they said the situation was "worse than they could have imagined" and called for greater regional and global effort to alleviate the suffering of Zimbabweans.{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/elders-zimbabwe-failing-its-people|title=The Elders: Zimbabwe is failing its people|website=The Elders|date=24 November 2008 }} Graça Machel said that "the state is no longer able to offer basic services. It can no longer feed, educate or care for its citizens. It is failing its people."{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2009/feb/01/zimbabwe-coalition-deal|title=Nelson Mandela's 'elders' welcome Zimbabwe's coalition deal|agency=Associated Press|date=1 February 2009|website=The Guardian}} Following the resignation of President [[Robert Mugabe]] in November, 2017 The Elders urged all stakeholders in Zimbabwe and the region to work together for a genuine democratic transition. In 2018 and beyond they will continue to stand in solidarity with the people of Zimbabwe, civil society and human rights defenders in holding the country's new leaders to account.{{cite web|url=https://www.theelders.org/zimbabwe|title=Zimbabwe|website=The Elders|access-date=2018-02-06|archive-date=7 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180207005016/https://www.theelders.org/zimbabwe|url-status=dead}} ====Child Marriage==== The Elders are committed to ending the practice of child marriage.{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-13681053|title=Ethiopian girls fight child marriages|first=Will|last=Ross|work=BBC News |date=7 June 2011}} In June 2011, Desmond Tutu, Gro Brundtland and Mary Robinson visited [[Amhara Region|Amhara, Ethiopia]], to learn about child marriage in a region where half of all female children are married before the age of 15. Alongside their fellow Elder Ela Bhatt, Tutu, Brundtland and Robinson also travelled to [[Bihar|Bihar, India]] in February 2012. Together, they visited Jagriti, a youth-led project aimed at preventing child marriage, and encouraged the state government's efforts to tackle the issue.{{cite web|url=http://www.womensviewsonnews.org/2011/09/girls-not-brides-an-end-to-child-marriages/|title=Girls not brides: an end to child marriages - Women's Views on News|website=www.womensviewsonnews.org}}{{cite news |title=Elders' advice: Stop child marriages - Times of India |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/patna/Elders-advice-Stop-child-marriages/articleshow/11801903.cms?referral=PM |website=[[The Times of India]]| date=8 February 2012 }} In 2011, The Elders initiated [[Girls Not Brides]]: The Global Partnership to End Child Marriage, which brings together civil society organisations from around the world that work to tackle child marriage.{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/girls-not-brides-new-global-partnership-end-child-marriage|title=Girls Not Brides – a new global partnership to end child marriage|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427100300/http://www.theelders.org/article/girls-not-brides-new-global-partnership-end-child-marriage|url-status=dead}} The global partnership aims to support activists working for change at the grassroots and call on governments and global organisations to make ending child marriage an international priority. Girls Not Brides became a fully independent organization, spun off from The Elders, in 2013. In July 2016, The Elders welcomed action taken by leaders in [[The Gambia]], [[Tanzania]] and [[Uganda]] to end child marriage, as part of the [[African Union]]'s continent-wide campaign to eradicate the harmful practice.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-welcome-new-moves-africa-end-child-marriage|title=The Elders welcome new moves in Africa to end child marriage|website=The Elders|date=15 July 2016 }} ====Côte d'Ivoire==== Following widespread violence after long-awaited presidential elections in November 2010, The Elders committed to support efforts by the Ivorian government and civil society to promote reconciliation and healing in the country. Desmond Tutu, Kofi Annan and Mary Robinson visited [[Ivory Coast]] on 1–2 May 2011 during which, they not only "encouraged reconciliation and healing", but they also emphasised the importance of improving the country's security situation. Beside meeting the President [[Alassane Ouattara]], Prime Minister [[Guillaume Soro]] and former President [[Laurent Gbagbo]],{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-visit-cote-divoire-encourage-healing-and-national-reconciliation|title=The Elders to visit Côte d'Ivoire to encourage healing and national reconciliation|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427100600/http://theelders.org/article/elders-visit-cote-divoire-encourage-healing-and-national-reconciliation|url-status=dead}} they also brought together civil society organisations, including women's groups seeking a role in the peace process, and encouraged them to work together towards national reconciliation.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-encourage-plans-truth-and-reconciliation-process-cote-divoire|title=The Elders encourage plans for truth and reconciliation process in Côte d'Ivoire|website=The Elders|access-date=18 August 2012|archive-date=1 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401210152/http://www.theelders.org/article/elders-encourage-plans-truth-and-reconciliation-process-cote-divoire|url-status=dead}} They also visited a camp for internally displaced people to hear directly from ordinary people affected by the conflict. Kofi Annan returned to Ivory Coast in January 2012 and October 2013 to support the ongoing reconciliation process. During his visit, he noted the progress that had been made and encouraged all Ivorians to participate in "the task of reconciliation and healing." in order to build an inclusive future and prepare for peaceful elections in 2015.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/media-advisory-kofi-annan-visit-cote-divoire-9-10-october-2013|title=Media advisory: Kofi Annan to visit Côte d'Ivoire from 9-10 October 2013|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2017|archive-date=27 April 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427100407/http://theelders.org/article/media-advisory-kofi-annan-visit-cote-divoire-9-10-october-2013|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/04/26/world/asia/26korea.html|title=Carter and Other Former Leaders to Travel to North Korea|first=Mark|last=McDonald|work=The New York Times |date=25 April 2011 }} ====Cyprus==== The Elders began working on [[Cyprus problem|Cyprus]] in September 2008, when the leaders of the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot communities formally entered into peace negotiations. Since then, they have visited the island four times to support all efforts to build peace, enhance trust, and sharing their experiences with leaders and civil society in order to encourage dialogue.{{cite web |url=http://theelders.org/cyprus |title=Cyprus |publisher=The Elders |access-date=2018-08-18 |archive-date=27 April 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427003748/http://theelders.org/cyprus |url-status=dead }} Additionally, they worked with the Committee on Missing Persons in Cyprus and the Cyprus Friendship Programme to film the documentary ''Digging the Past in Search of the Future'' with the hope that this could help Cypriots to reach a common understanding about their shared past.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/cyprus-digging-past-search-future|title=Cyprus: Digging the Past in Search of the Future|website=The Elders|date=30 August 2011 }} In October 2008, the Elders visited the island to support the newly begun peace talks between the Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders. Desmond Tutu said that "These opportunities don't come around very often".{{cite web|url=http://www.cyprusedirectory.com/articleview.aspx?ID=4375|title=Elders arrive to lend their moral support - Cyprus Internet Directory|access-date=25 March 2013|archive-date=21 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160121074541/http://www.cyprusedirectory.com/articleview.aspx?ID=4375|url-status=dead}} Elders Jimmy Carter, Lakhdar Brahimi and Desmond Tutu met political leaders, civil society representatives and young people from both communities.{{cite web|url=https://usatoday30.usatoday.com/news/world/2008-10-08-1893099243_x.htm|title=World peacemakers offer support for Cyprus talks - USATODAY.com|website=usatoday30.usatoday.com}} Throughout the visit they made it clear that they were visiting the island to offer support and not to get formally involvement in the peace process. Gro Harlem Brundtland and Lakhdar Brahimi visited [[Athens]], [[Ankara]] and [[Cyprus]] in September 2009 to encourage efforts to reunify the island. In Ankara they met Turkish President [[Abdullah Gül]],{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/cyprus-peace-process-going-well-facing-challenges|title=Cyprus peace process going well, but facing challenges|website=The Elders|date=11 September 2009 }} and Greek Prime Minister [[George Papandreou]] in Athens. In [[Nicosia]] they met Turkish Cypriot leader [[Mehmet Ali Talat]] and the President of the Republic of Cyprus [[Demetris Christofias|Demitris Christofias]].{{cite web|url=http://www.cyprusedirectory.com/articleview.aspx?ID=14527|title=The Elders in Cyprus to help peace process - Cyprus Internet Directory|access-date=25 March 2013|archive-date=21 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160121074541/http://www.cyprusedirectory.com/articleview.aspx?ID=14527|url-status=dead}} The Elders also met local media and leading women from politics, business and civil society on the island.{{cite web|url=http://www.cyprusedirectory.com/cyprusguide/cyprus.aspx?ID=14551|title=Elders: Cypriot media 'scathing and pessimistic' – Cyprus Guide|access-date=25 March 2013|archive-date=21 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160121074541/http://www.cyprusedirectory.com/cyprusguide/cyprus.aspx?ID=14551|url-status=dead}} In December 2009, Desmond Tutu, Jimmy Carter and Lakhdar Brahimi returned to Cyprus. They convened a public meeting on how trust could be engendered between conflicting communities and together with the Committee on Missing Persons filmed the documentary, ''Cyprus: Digging the Past in Search of the Future''.{{cite web | title=Cyprus: Digging the Past in Search of the Future | website=The Elders | date=August 30, 2011 | url=https://theelders.org/news/cyprus-digging-past-search-future | access-date=May 24, 2026}} The documentary follows the three Elders as they accompany four young Cypriots to learn about the search for the remains of thousands of missing people who were killed in the violence of the 1960s and 1970s.{{cite web|url=http://www.hri.org/news/cyprus/cna/2011/11-02-08_1.cna.html|title=Cyprus News Agency: News in English, 11-02-08|website=www.hri.org}} It was launched in early 2011 with special screenings in Nicosia and at the Houses of Parliament in London.. In Cyprus, Desmond Tutu and Gro Brundtland also met the newly elected leader of the Turkish Cypriot community, [[Derviş Eroğlu]] and the leader of the Greek Cypriot community, [[Demetris Christofias]], and called for a renewed spirit of leadership in Cyprus. The Elders also met the Archbishop of the Church of Cyprus, Chrysostomos II, to discuss the role of religious leaders in peacebuilding. ====Korean Peninsula==== The Elders launched their [[Korea|Korean Peninsula]] initiative in April 2011, when a delegation led by Jimmy Carter made a six-day visit to the [[Republic of Korea]] (South Korea), the [[Democratic People's Republic of Korea]] (North Korea) and [[China]].{{cite web|url=http://www.aljazeera.com/news/asia-pacific/2011/04/201142634658654793.html|title=Carter leads North Korea peace mission|website=www.aljazeera.com}} Jimmy Carter, together with Martti Ahtisaari, Gro Harlem Brundtland and Mary Robinson, aimed to alleviate tensions on the Peninsula, particularly by encouraging dialogue and addressing security and humanitarian concerns such as reported food shortages in North Korea.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/qa-elders-visit-korean-peninsula|title=Q&A: The Elders' visit to the Korean Peninsula|website=The Elders|access-date=25 March 2013|archive-date=13 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130513002512/http://theelders.org/article/qa-elders-visit-korean-peninsula|url-status=dead}} In all three countries, they met senior government officials, diplomats, UN representatives, humanitarian agencies, researchers, think tanks and [[North Korean defectors|North Korean refugees]] who fled to South Korea. Throughout the visit they made it clear that they were acting independently and did not intend "to replace or intervene in any official process".{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/report-elders-visit-korean-peninsula-and-china-april-2011|title=Report: The Elders' visit to the Korean Peninsula and China, April 2011|website=The Elders|date=6 January 2011 }} In a report released following the Elders' visit, Jimmy Carter stated: "On relations between North and South Korea, there are no quick fixes...and progress will require greater flexibility, sincerity and commitment from all parties".{{cite web|url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/nation/2011/07/113_91703.html|title=The Elders hail talks with N. Korea|date=27 July 2011}} Martti Ahtisaari and Gro Harlem Brundtland later travelled to Brussels to brief senior European Union officials on their findings. ====Sudan and South Sudan==== Peace in Sudan became a top priority for The Elders as soon as the group was founded. Indeed, The Elders' first mission was to [[Sudan]], from 30 September to 4 October 2007. Desmond Tutu, Lakhdar Brahimi, Jimmy Carter and Graça Machel travelled to the country to learn more about the humanitarian situation in [[Darfur]] and to affirm the group's support for the [[Comprehensive Peace Agreement]] (CPA), which was negotiated between [[The Sudans|North and South Sudan]] in 2005 to end its 22-year [[Second Sudanese Civil War|civil war.]] The Elders published a report on their findings titled 'Bringing Hope, Forging Peace: The Elders' Mission to Sudan'.{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/sudan-south-sudan|title=Sudan & South Sudan|website=The Elders}} In 2008, the Elders encouraged states to provide urgently needed helicopters for peacekeepers in Darfur.{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/humanitarian-situation-will-deteriorate-sharply-sudan-after-expulsion-aid-workers|title=Humanitarian situation will deteriorate sharply in Sudan after expulsion of aid workers|website=The Elders}} In March 2009 the Elders called for aid agencies to be given access to Sudan following their expulsion by the Sudanese government.{{cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/desmond-tutu/sudan-between-peril-and-h_b_423300.html|title=Sudan Between Peril and Hope|first1=Desmond|last1=Tutu|first2=Lakhdar|last2=Brahimi|website=[[HuffPost]] |date=18 March 2010}} Ahead of [[South Sudan]]'s self-determination referendum in January 2011, The Elders warned of a risk of renewed violence in Sudan and urged 'swift and bold action' by the international community in support of the peace process.{{cite web|url=https://www.cartercenter.org/news/pr/sudan-010311.html|title=Jimmy Carter, Kofi Annan, Joseph Warioba, and John Hardman to Lead Carter Center Delegation to Observe Referendum on Self-Determination of Southern Sudan|website=www.cartercenter.org}} Particularly, Jimmy Carter and Kofi Annan led the Carter Center delegation to observe the [[2011 South Sudanese independence referendum|referendum on self-determination in South Sudan.]]{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/elders-sudan-and-south-sudan-initiative-2012|title=The Elders' Sudan and South Sudan initiative, 2012|website=The Elders|date=17 October 2012 }} In 2012, prompted by the "worsening relations between Sudan and South Sudan, deteriorating economic conditions in both countries, and renewed conflict in the Sudanese states of [[Blue Nile (state)|Blue Nile]] and [[South Kordofan]]", The Elders decided to make a series of visits to Sudan, South Sudan and Ethiopia.{{cite web|url=http://www.sudantribune.com/Sudan-is-willing-to-withdraw-its,42725|title=Sudan is willing to withdraw its troops from Abyei, President Carter – ''Sudan Tribune'': Plural news and views on Sudan|website=www.sudantribune.com}} They aimed to highlight the growing humanitarian crisis and encourage further peace talks between the governments of Sudan and South Sudan. In May 2012, Lakhdar Brahimi and Jimmy Carter met Sudanese President [[Omar al-Bashir]] in Khartoum.{{cite web|url=http://www.unhcr.org/4ffb07349.html|title=The Elders visit Sudanese refugees on peace errand|first=United Nations High Commissioner for|last=Refugees}} In July 2012, Martti Ahtisaari, Mary Robinson and Desmond Tutu travelled to South Sudan to meet President [[Salva Kiir Mayardit|Salva Kiir]] and civil society representatives, and to visit Yusuf Batil refugee camp near the border with Sudan.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-congratulate-south-sudan-first-anniversary-independence|title=The Elders congratulate South Sudan on first anniversary of independence|website=The Elders|access-date=25 April 2013|archive-date=1 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130201083012/http://www.theelders.org/article/elders-congratulate-south-sudan-first-anniversary-independence|url-status=dead}} They also travelled to Ethiopia, where they met [[Hailemariam Desalegn]] and members of the [[African Union]] High-Level Implementation Panel on Sudan (AUHIP), including [[Thabo Mbeki]] and [[Pierre Buyoya]]. At the conclusion of their visit, Ahtisaari, Tutu and Robinson urged presidents Bashir and Kiir to meet as soon as possible and recommit to peace. Desmond Tutu stated: "Peace, peace, peace is what the people of Sudan and South Sudan need most. Recent months have seen increased hardship and suffering in both countries. It is a fragile time and I hope that the leaders will do what their people need, which is to recommit to working together to build two viable states."{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2008/nov/15/zimbabwe-united-nations-kofi-annan|title=Annan to lead team on humanitarian mission to Harare|first=Xan|last=Rice|date=15 November 2008|website=the Guardian}} ====Sri Lanka==== The Elders have closely followed developments in [[Sri Lanka]] and spoken out on several occasions since the end of the [[Sri Lankan civil war|decades-long conflict]] in 2009. Particularly, The Elders have persistently emphasised the importance of achieving reconciliation and accountability for violations committed during the conflict. In November 2009, the Elders wrote to Sri Lankan [[Mahinda Rajapaksa|President Rajapaksa]]{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-call-sri-lankan-government-protect-rights-civilians-displaced-conflict|title=The Elders call on Sri Lankan government to protect rights of civilians displaced by conflict|website=The Elders|date=26 November 2009 }} as well as major donors, calling on the government to protect the rights of displaced civilians following years of war. Desmond Tutu said the government had "an obligation to serve all Sri Lanka's citizens – including the Tamil and other minority communities".{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-south-asia-10851163|title=Elders group criticises Sri Lanka|first=Saroj|last=Pathirana|work=BBC News |date=3 August 2010}} In August 2010, The Elders expressed disappointment at the Sri Lankan government's clampdown on domestic critics and "disdain for human rights". The Elders added that meaningful progress on reconciliation on the island was still "desperately needed".{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2012/feb/26/our-duty-sri-lanka-human-rights|title=Our duty to Sri Lanka, and human rights - Desmond Tutu and Mary Robinson|first1=Desmond|last1=Tutu|first2=Mary|last2=Robinson|date=26 February 2012|website=the Guardian}} In February 2012, Mary Robinson and Desmond Tutu wrote an op-ed in ''[[The Guardian]]'', urging the member states of the [[United Nations Human Rights Council]] "to support a resolution that seeks accountability for the terrible violations of international law that have taken place, and establishes mechanisms to monitor progress on the steps the government is taking on accountability".{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/03/23/world/asia/rights-body-passes-measure-on-sri-lanka.html|title=U.N. Rights Council Passes Sri Lanka Resolution|first=Nick|last=Cumming-Bruce|work=The New York Times |date=22 March 2012 }} The U.S.-backed resolution on 'Promoting reconciliation and accountability in Sri Lanka' was adopted by the Council on 22 March 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/sri-lanka-needs-know-world-watching|title=Sri Lanka needs to know the world is watching|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2013|archive-date=9 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130509031907/http://theelders.org/article/sri-lanka-needs-know-world-watching|url-status=dead}} Robinson and Tutu wrote a further op-ed published in ''[[The Times]]'', ''[[The Times of India]]'' and the ''[[Tribune de Genève]]'' in March 2013, calling on the Council and the [[Commonwealth of Nations|Commonwealth]] to exert pressure on Sri Lanka's government to implement the recommendations of the [[Lessons Learnt and Reconciliation Commission]] (LLRC).{{cite web|url=http://reliefweb.int/report/sudan/bringing-hope-forging-peace-elders-mission-sudan|title=Bringing hope, forging peace - The Elders' mission to Sudan|date=30 November 2007 }} ===Other activities=== The organisation has also issued statements on a range of topics including those relating to [[Tibet]],{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/pakistan-floods-elders-urge-world-respond-more-quickly-and-generously|title=PAKISTAN FLOODS: The Elders urge the world to respond more quickly and generously|website=The Elders|date=19 August 2010 }} [[Pakistan]],{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/elders-condemn-deadly-attacks-norway|title=The Elders condemn deadly attacks in Norway|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2013|archive-date=6 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131206221129/http://theelders.org/article/elders-condemn-deadly-attacks-norway|url-status=dead}} [[Norway]],{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/ela-bhatt-urges-partnership-poor-opening-un-meeting-mdgs|title=Ela Bhatt urges 'partnership with the poor' at opening of UN meeting on MDGs|website=The Elders|date=25 September 2008 }} the [[International Criminal Court]],{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-urge-all-states-commit-universal-impartial-international-criminal-court|title=The Elders urge all states to commit to universal, impartial International Criminal Court|website=The Elders|date=26 October 2016 }} and the [[Millennium Development Goals]].{{cite web|url=http://russia-insider.com/en/politics/world-influencers-elders-meet-moscow/6306|title=World Influencers "The Elders" Meet in Moscow|date=1 May 2015}} ====Kenya==== Widespread violence erupted in [[Kenya]] in December 2007, following disputes over the results of national elections. In January 2008, the African Union established a Panel of Eminent African Personalities to mediate a solution to the crisis, headed by Kofi Annan and including Graça Machel and former Tanzanian Prime Minister [[Benjamin Mkapa]]. Earlier, the Kenyan churches had launched an unsuccessful mediation attempt headed by South African Archbishop and Elders chair, Desmond Tutu. While three Elders were involved in efforts to resolve Kenya's crisis, this was not an initiative of The Elders.{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/elders-peaceful-solutions-must-be-sought-kenya|title=The Elders: Peaceful solutions must be sought in Kenya|website=The Elders|date=5 January 2008 }} The Elders issued a brief statement in January 2008 calling for an end to the violence. ====Middle East and North Africa==== Following [[Arab Spring|major demonstrations across the Middle East and North Africa]] in 2011, The Elders stated that they stood in solidarity with "all those crying out for freedom and basic rights". In an interview with CNN, Desmond Tutu called on the international community to bring pressure to bear on [[Muammar Gaddafi]] to relinquish power.{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/elders-begin-two-day-visit-egypt|title=The Elders begin two-day visit to Egypt|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2013|archive-date=3 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203045921/http://www.theelders.org/article/elders-begin-two-day-visit-egypt|url-status=dead}} In November 2011, a few weeks after elections to Tunisia's Constituent Assembly, Martti Ahtisaari, Mary Robinson and Lakhdar Brahimi travelled to [[Tunis]] to attend the annual gathering of the [[Mo Ibrahim Foundation]]. In an interview with the BBC following her meeting with Tunisian bloggers, Mary Robinson described the "sense of buoyant democracy" in the country. Gro Harlem Brundtland, Jimmy Carter and Mary Robinson travelled to [[Cairo]] in October 2012. During their meetings with President [[Mohamed Morsi]], senior officials and diplomats, representatives of civil society organisations and young people, the Elders emphasised the importance of "an inclusive, democratic transition."{{cite web|url=http://www.theelders.org/article/egypt-transition-elders-visit-cairo|title=Egypt in transition: Elders visit Cairo|website=The Elders|access-date=26 April 2013|archive-date=3 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203045750/http://www.theelders.org/article/egypt-transition-elders-visit-cairo|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cartercenter.org/news/trip_reports/egypt-011712.html|title=Trip Report by Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter to Egypt, Jan. 8-14, 2012|website=www.cartercenter.org}} Brundtland and Carter both visited Egypt earlier in 2012, where they met civil society organisations and spoke to students at the [[The American University in Cairo|American University in Cairo]]. Carter also travelled to Egypt with the [[Carter Center]] to witness the country's [[2012 Egyptian presidential election|presidential]] and parliamentary elections in January{{cite web|url=https://www.cartercenter.org/news/trip_reports/egypt-0529.html|title=Trip Report by Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter to Egypt, May 21-28, 2012|website=www.cartercenter.org}} and May 2012. Outside of their role as Elders, Kofi Annan and Lakhdar Brahimi have individually been involved in the international efforts to try to resolve the conflict in [[Syria]]. In February 2012, Annan was appointed Joint Special Envoy of the United Nations and [[League of Arab States]] on the [[Syrian civil war|Syrian Civil War]].{{cite web|url=https://www.un.org/apps/news/story.asp?NewsID=42702#.WQDDGFPyvJO|title=UN, Arab League appoint veteran diplomat to take over Annan's role on Syrian crisis|date=17 August 2012}} He was succeeded in the role by Brahimi, who was appointed Joint Special Representative in August 2012, a position he held until May 2014. ====Russia==== The Elders held a three-day visit to [[Moscow]] in April 2015. Kofi Annan, Gro Harlem Brundtland, Martti Ahtisaari, Lakhdar Brahimi, Jimmy Carter and Ernesto Zedillo held talks on geopolitical issues with Russian officials, including [[President Putin]], Foreign Minister [[Lavrov]] and former Soviet President [[Mikhail Gorbachev]].{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-conclude-three-day-visit-moscow|title=The Elders conclude three-day visit to Moscow|website=The Elders|date=29 April 2015 }} ===Campaigns=== ===State of Hope=== In July 2021, The Elders launched the "State of Hope" series of digital discussions to explore significant global challenges. Mary Robinson, Graça Machel, Juan Manuel Santos, Ban Ki-moon and Zeid Raad Al Hussein delivered online addresses on the relationship between hope, peace, justice, human rights and multilateralism.{{cite web | title=State of Hope - The Elders | website=The Elders | url=https://stateofhope.live/ | language=en-US | access-date=May 24, 2026}} Their speeches were complemented by video responses from selected global figures including former UK Prime Minister [[Gordon Brown]], NASA astronaut [[Chris Hadfield]] and Ugandan climate activist [[Vanessa Nakate]]. ===Finding Humanity podcasts=== During the initial phase of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], The Elders produced a special podcast series called "Finding Humanity",{{cite web | website=Finding Humanity podcast | title=Elder Series | url=https://findinghumanitypodcast.com/episodes#elders-series}} focusing on the need for empathetic and principled leadership on some of the biggest challenges facing humanity. In episodes broadcast from 2020 to 2021, topics included pandemic preparedness, access to justice, ending violence against women and girls, reform of the UN Security Council, and the existential threat posed by nuclear weapons. The Finding Humanity series was produced by the Humanity Lab Foundation and Hueman Group Media in partnership with The Elders, and was hosted by [[Hazami Barmada]], Founder of the Humanity Lab Foundation. ====#WalkTogether==== Together with civil society partners, The Elders marked their 10th anniversary by launching #WalkTogether, a year-long global campaign to inspire hope and bridge the deepening global fault lines of division, hate and xenophobia. The campaign is intended to celebrate those communities whose work is a great demonstration of empathy, where their actions benefit 'the many', create a sense of unity, and address global and local challenges in a compassionate way. In other words, #WalkTogether aims to lift the voices of courageous moral leadership in communities around the world, who are working for the freedoms aligned to those to which Nelson Mandela dedicated his life. These freedoms] include the broad themes of peace, health, justice and equality.{{cite web | title=Freedoms | website=#WalkTogether | date=June 23, 2022 | url=https://www.walk-together.org/freedoms/ | access-date=May 24, 2026 | url-status=usurped | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171006211737/https://www.walk-together.org/freedoms/ | archive-date=October 6, 2017}} The campaign ran for twelve months from 18 July 2017 – the tenth anniversary of the group's founding – to 18 July 2018, the centenary of Nelson Mandela's birth.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/walk-together|title=Walk Together|website=The Elders|access-date=6 October 2017|archive-date=6 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171006212222/http://theelders.org/walk-together|url-status=dead}} ====Every Human Has Rights==== The Every Human Has Rights (EHHR) campaign was launched on the 60th anniversary of the [[Universal Declaration of Human Rights]] (UDHR), 10 December 2007, in [[Cape Town]], [[South Africa]]. The Elders launched the initiative in partnership with a diverse group of global NGOs, civil society organisations and businesses to highlight UDHR principles, including the [[right to health]], women's rights, and freedom of expression. Launch partners included [[ActionAid]], [[Amnesty International]], the [[Center for Women's Global Leadership]], [[International PEN]], WITNESS, Realizing Rights, [[Save the Children]] and [[UNICEF]]. The EHHR campaign also included partners from civil society organisations in the developing world through networks like [[CIVICUS]]. The campaign aimed to "empower global citizens to protect and realize the first-ever comprehensive agreement on [[human rights]] among nations". Throughout the campaign, over one billion people signed the Universal Declaration, taking responsibility and pledging to speak to protect the freedom and the rights of others in their communities.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/elders-launch-every-human-has-rights-campaign|title=The Elders launch the Every Human Has Rights campaign|website=The Elders|date=10 December 2007 }} A year later, in December 2008, The Elders joined award-winning human rights journalists, leaders in civil society, and business and government leaders to celebrate the Every Human Has Rights campaign and participate in the EHHR Media Awards.{{cite web|url=http://theelders.org/article/every-human-has-rights-media-awards|title=Every Human Has Rights Media Awards|website=The Elders|date=6 December 2008 }} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category|The Elders (organisation)}} * [http://www.theelders.org/ The Elders' official website] {{The Elders|state=expanded}} {{Nelson Mandela}} {{Jimmy Carter}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Elders (Organization), The}} [[Category:The Elders (organization)| ]] [[Category:Peace organizations]] [[Category:International human rights organizations]] [[Category:Political organizations established in 2007]] [[Category:Non-profit organisations based in London]]
extract: The Elders is an international non-governmental organisation of public figures noted as senior statesmen, peace activists and human rights advocates, who were brought together by former president of South Africa Nelson Mandela in 2007. They describe themselves as "independent global leaders working together for peace, justice, human rights and a sustainable planet". The goal Mandela set for The Elders was to use their "almost 1,000 years of collective experience" to work on solutions for seemingly insurmountable problems such as climate change, HIV/AIDS, and poverty, as well as to "use their political independence to help resolve some of the world's most intractable conflicts".
